Maintenance Report — MNT-0110-005

Asset: WELL-0110 (NE-07 Well 110, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 09 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 10 Jun 2023 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 24 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0110-0034 on 2023-06-08 Report written: 12 Jun 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0110-0034 at 13:15 on 2023-06-08 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.1% of the pad area, estimated 4.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 216 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 173 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.8 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0110-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.35% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0110-017

Asset: WELL-0110 (NE-07 Well 110, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 08 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 12 Mar 2025 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 107 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0110-0124 on 2025-03-06 Report written: 14 Mar 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0110-0124 showed the wellhead at 10.8 °C with the air at 10.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
